xmldoc.short_description: Selected singular values and singular vectors of a sparse matrix.

param_input_item.param_description: a sparse double, single, complex double, or complex single matrix.
a positive integer smaller than the smaller matrix dimension. Default is 6.
a string: 'largest' or 'lm' for largest singular values, 'smallest' or 'sm' for smallest singular values.

param_output_item.param_description: selected singular values returned as a dense column vector in decreasing order.
dense matrix whose columns are the selected left singular vectors.
dense diagonal matrix containing the selected singular values.
dense matrix whose columns are the selected right singular vectors.

description.p: svds computes selected singular values and, optionally, the corresponding singular vectors of a sparse floating-point matrix.
For a matrix A, the returned factors satisfy:
Tall matrices use the smaller normal problem when possible, and wide matrices use the corresponding transposed normal problem.
When the optional ARPACK backend is not available, svds uses a dense fallback for small sparse matrices. Larger sparse matrices still require ARPACK to avoid excessive memory use.

Sparse single and sparse single-complex inputs are accepted. The selected singular-value problem is computed through the double-precision sparse backend, and dense outputs are converted back to single or single-complex when applicable.

history_item.history_description: dense fallback added for small sparse matrices when ARPACK is unavailable.
sparse single and sparse single-complex inputs supported through the sparse double-precision backend.
